items.metric: Transport CPI vs Restaurants & Accommodation CPI, annual
items.change: transport up from +15.7% in August; headline 7.3%, a three-year high
items.note: REFRESHED 5 NOV 2026. Headline 7.3% (6.8% September). Food and non-alcoholic beverages +10.2%; housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels +3.7%. CBK splits it as core 4.3% (4.0%) and NON-CORE 15.1% (14.0%): the pressure is fuel, transport and food, the lines a kitchen, laundry and transfer fleet carry. Overall index 156.47 to 157.60 (+0.7% m/m, Citizen Digital). The KNBS restaurants-and-accommodation line for October was NOT found in any source we could read (KNBS PDF blocks our crawler), so no real room-price figure is given this month; August's was -3.6pp.
items.source: KNBS October 2026 CPI, released 30 Oct 2026, via Kenyans.co.ke (30 Oct) and Citizen Digital (31 Oct); core/non-core: CBK Weekly Bulletin, 30 Oct 2026 (read at primary)

items.note: REFRESHED 5 NOV 2026. Headline 5.8% (4.6% September) and core 4.4% (3.7%) are double-sourced. Food crops +10.7% (4.5%); energy, fuel and utilities +15.4% (14.5%); diesel +49.2% year on year (Nile Post). items.metric: Transport CPI vs Restaurants & Hotels CPI, annual (urban)
items.change: urban headline 19.5%, up from 17.2% in September
items.note: REFRESHED 16 NOV 2026 FROM THE NISR OCTOBER REPORT (primary, 10 Nov). Urban CPI 19.5%; rural 31.3%; all-Rwanda 26.5%; core 11.5%; urban prices +3.3% in the month. Urban food +28.9%. Restaurants and hotels +20.6% (+2.7% m/m) now trail the urban headline: a real room-price change of about +1.1pp, down from +1.7pp in September (our arithmetic). PREVIOUS: REFRESHED 5 NOV 2026 FROM THE NISR REPORT. Urban CPI 17.2%; rural 22.0%; all-Rwanda 20.0%; core 11.4%. Urban food +20.9%; housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels +18.3%. Restaurants and hotels (+18.9%) are now rising FASTER than the urban headline: a real room-price change of +1.7pp (our arithmetic), against -0.1pp in August. Rwanda remains the one market where operators are passing the cost shock through. October CPI is due about 10 November.
items.source: NISR, Consumer Price Index October 2026, published 10 Nov 2026 (read at primary)

items.change: unchanged at the 14 Nov review (landed cost +6.11%)
items.note: RETAINED 14 NOV 2026 for 15 Nov–14 Dec (EPRA, primary). Landed cost rose 6.11% (US$977.55 to 1,037.30/m³); the government drew KSh 4.6bn from the Petroleum Development Levy fund, absorbing about KSh 8.58/L that would otherwise have reached the pump. Mombasa KSh 223.81. Prices include 8% VAT. Next review 14 Dec, effective 15 Dec. PREVIOUS CYCLE: CORRECTED 5 NOV 2026: this row showed the 15 Sep–14 Oct price (KSh 214.03) for three weeks after EPRA raised it. EPRA attributed the rise to higher import costs from the Middle East conflict. Mombasa KSh 223.80/L (HapaKenya). VAT on fuel stays at 8%: the Tax Laws (Amendment) Act extended the reduced rate for 90 days from 15 Oct (KBC, 16 Oct; Kenyans.co.ke, 15 Oct), so the feared VAT step-up did not land. Next review 14 Nov, effective 15 Nov.
items.source: EPRA, Maximum Retail Petroleum Prices in Kenya for 15 Nov–14 Dec 2026, 14 Nov 2026 (read at primary); subsidy figures: Citizen Digital, TV47 and Kenyans.co.ke (14 Nov 2026)

items.change: unchanged at the 14 Nov review (landed cost +6.73%)
items.note: RETAINED 14 NOV 2026 for 15 Nov–14 Dec (EPRA, primary). Landed cost rose 6.73% (US$1,065.38 to 1,137.09/m³); the levy fund absorbed about KSh 10.54/L. Mombasa KSh 224.71. The cushion is deferred cost, not relief: keep the fuel-adjustment clause in transfer contracts. PREVIOUS CYCLE: CORRECTED 5 NOV 2026 (was KSh 217.86). Diesel is the safari cost driver: game drives, transfers, generators, borehole pumps and supply runs. The deferred landed-cost rise flagged in September has now reached the pump. Mombasa KSh 224.48/L (HapaKenya). Note that HapaKenya reports the diesel rise as KSh 12.04; The Star's KSh 9.90 matches our recorded prior price, and both give the same new cap. Supplier fuel surcharges dated from 15 Oct are legitimate; re-quote Q4 transfer supplements against 227.76 and keep a fuel-adjustment clause, since Murban was above US$110/bbl in late October.
items.source: EPRA, Maximum Retail Petroleum Prices in Kenya for 15 Nov–14 Dec 2026, 14 Nov 2026 (read at primary); subsidy figures: Citizen Digital, TV47 and Kenyans.co.ke (14 Nov 2026)

items.change: unchanged at the 14 Nov review (landed cost +0.71%)

items.change: -USD 3.97 week on week (94.04 on 5 Nov); about 18% below the late-October peak of 110.46
items.note: REFRESHED 16 NOV 2026 (CBK Weekly Bulletin, week ending 13 Nov, primary). Falling crude plus a levy-funded cushion of KSh 8.58 (petrol) and 10.54 (diesel) per litre means the 14 Dec review could unwind the subsidy without a pump rise; our reading, not an EPRA forecast. REFRESHED 9 NOV 2026: Murban fell about 15% in the week to 5 Nov, from US$110.46 to US$94.04 (CBK Weekly Bulletin, 6 Nov, primary). This weakens the case for a large rise at the 14 Nov EPRA review, but EPRA's formula uses landed costs over the prior cycle, so the October spike still feeds in; our reading, not an EPRA forecast. PREVIOUS NOTE: CORRECTED 5 NOV 2026: this row showed USD 67.99 from July. Murban is the crude Kenya's landed cost tracks. At about US$110 it is more than 60% above the July reading, and CBK says October pump prices rose on higher international oil prices. This points to upward pressure at the 14 Nov EPRA review; our reading, not a forecast from EPRA.
items.source: CBK Weekly Bulletin, week ending 13 Nov 2026 (read at primary)

items.change: fuel energy cost charge KSh 3.22/unit + forex adjustment KSh 0.87/unit; down from over KSh 5.00 in July
items.note: CORRECTED 16 NOV 2026: this row showed July's figure for three months. EPRA's notice of 9 Oct set the fuel energy cost charge at KSh 3.22/kWh (plus a water levy of 1.34 cents) on October meter readings and the forex adjustment at 87 cents on September readings (Kenyans.co.ke, 10 Oct; Capital FM, 11 Oct). No November notice was found as at 16 Nov, and the EPRA notice itself was not read. PREVIOUS NOTE: CARRIED OVER, NOT RE-CHECKED SINCE JULY 2026 (tracker refresh 5 Nov 2026). With crude now near US$110 the fuel energy cost charge is likely to have moved; check the latest EPRA Gazette pass-through notice before quoting. The quiet margin killer: the monthly fuel-energy-cost and forex-adjustment charges added more than KSh 5 to every unit in July. Read the pass-through line on the bill, not the tariff band.
items.source: EPRA pass-through notice of 9 Oct 2026, via Kenyans.co.ke (10 Oct 2026) and Capital FM (11 Oct 2026); EPRA notice not read

items.metric: Bank of Uganda Central Bank Rate
items.change: held at the 9 Nov MPC (+225bp from 9.75% at the 14 Oct emergency MPC)
items.note: HELD AT 12% ON 9 NOV 2026 (Daily Monitor, 9 Nov; The Rio Times, 9 Nov; BoU's own statement not found). Next meeting date not published. ADDED 5 NOV 2026. An emergency hike, the first move since October 2024, citing shilling depreciation, a wider external deficit and imported-inflation risk from the Middle East conflict. The shilling hit 4,143/US$, its weakest since 1993, and BoU sold about US$30m to pull it back under 4,000 (Daily Monitor, 16 Oct; single source for the FX figures). For Ugandan operators: USD rate cards gain in shilling terms, but imported F&B, fuel and spares cost more, and shilling borrowing is dearer.
items.source: Nairametrics (14 Oct 2026); Daily Monitor (16 Oct 2026); hold: Daily Monitor and The Rio Times (9 Nov 2026)

items.note: REFRESHED 16 NOV 2026 (NISR October report, primary, 10 Nov): urban 19.5%, rural 31.3%, all-Rwanda 26.5%, core 11.5%, urban m/m +3.3%. NISR names urban as the headline; some outlets (Ecofin, The Rio Times) mislabel 19.5% as all-Rwanda. PREVIOUS: REFRESHED 5 NOV 2026 (row previously showed June's 13.6%). Rural 22.0%, all-Rwanda 20.0%, core 11.4%. Urban inflation has risen every month since March (9.2%). A Kigali property holding its 2025 USD rate card into 2027 is absorbing a high-teens local cost increase against a flat nominal cross-rate. Rebuild the rate card rather than indexing it.
